status: form decided 2026-11-19: A = DSH native plugin (no MCP). The eight named tools below stay the canonical ACTION surface; the host projection (see hostProjection) exposes them as one tool with an action discriminator, which is this host's convention for a multi-action capability.

hostProjection.why: root cause: five resident tool schemas describing one engine is a standing per-turn token cost with no added capability; the host's own shell/terminal tools are one-tool-with-action. The action surface here is unchanged -- same actions, same arguments, same refusal codes (0.5.0 added three read-only actions to the SAME one tool, so the token argument still holds).

extraWorkerActions.why: protocol/encoding self-test; not part of the tool surface
owner control, behind the settings pill rather than the model's reach

notes: The eight tool names are fixed here so both delivery forms expose the same action surface.
src/engine/engine.ps1 is the only implementation; this file is the contract, not a second implementation.
docs/refusals.md is the human-readable form of `refusals`; scripts/check-refusals.mjs keeps them equal.
The `refusalCases` array is executable: test/refusals-test.ps1 iterates it and binds the placeholders, so a documented refusal path cannot rot into fiction.

0.5.0 adds snapshot/screenshot/preview. They are READ paths: `snapshot` walks the accessibility tree and hands the model numbered `label`s, `screenshot` captures the window rect and returns the coordinate mapping as data, `preview` draws the marker at a point and reports the element UNDER it as text. No new input primitive, no automatic fallback chain -- the model decides.

stance.inputQueue: quiet and bounded-flash tiers write nothing to the OS input queue. The takeover tier (opt-in, takeoverAllowed) may send KEYBOARD input (SendInput + KEYEVENTF_UNICODE) only when keyInput='inject' was requested; mouse injection is structurally impossible (MOUSEEVENTF_* is banned repo-wide and the gate enforces it)
stance.focus: no forged Alt key, no synthetic activation code. The bounded-flash tier reverses its one flash; the takeover tier holds the focus until the action ends and then restores it through the same table
stance.cursor: the cursor is 0 px in the quiet and bounded-flash tiers (24 measured rounds, scripts/channel-raise-matrix.ps1). The takeover tier moves it to the action point BY REQUEST and always restores it; a restore that fails is reported as cursorRestored=false and turns proof=fail
stance.keyboard: keyboard injection exists only inside the takeover tier, only for targets with no message door and no UIA pattern (terminals, measured), only after asserting GetForegroundWindow() is the target. It does not carry hardware scancodes (KEYEVENTF_UNICODE), so a target that reads scancodes only will ignore it -- documented, not a bug
stance.tiers: quiet (window messages) preferred over bounded-flash (UIA patterns) preferred over takeover (explicit request, HUD mandatory, always restored); the flash tier must reverse itself once and never pulls focus from a window the owner chose
stance.hud: the takeover tier cannot run without the HUD: it is a hard precondition (refuse takeover_unavailable), not a decoration. Three phases (arming/active/done), no-activate, click-through outside its button, and three independent interruption paths

tools.name: wpm_windows
tools.description: List live top-level windows the engine could drive: hwnd, title, window class, owning pid and screen rect. Read-only. Visible, titled, non-minimized windows only, because a list padded with invisible helper windows makes target selection guesswork.
tools.noRefusalReason: pure enumeration: no target is acted on, so there is nothing to refuse. An empty list means no window matched the filter, and that is reported as an empty list, not as a failure.

tools.name: wpm_click
tools.description: Click at a screen coordinate inside the named window, or at the element named by a snapshot `label`. Chooses the cheapest available door: a classic child window receives the click as a window message (quiet tier, measured 0/6 foreground changes), otherwise a UIA pattern is used and the foreground is reversed once afterwards (bounded-flash tier, measured net return 15..95 ms). The cursor does not move in either tier. With `space:"image"` the coordinates are IMAGE pixels from a `screenshot` and the engine converts them back to screen pixels -- the caller never multiplies a scale factor.

hwnd.description: Target top-level window handle, as returned by wpm_windows.

x.description: Screen X coordinate (or image X with space:'image'). Must resolve to a child window of the target, otherwise the action is refused instead of being sent somewhere else.

y.description: Screen Y coordinate (or image Y with space:'image').

space.description: Coordinate space of x/y. 'screen' (default) is physical screen pixels. 'image' means image pixels from the screenshot named by shotId; the engine converts them and still applies the point-ownership assertion, so a conversion bug cannot send the click to another window.

shotId.description: The shotId returned by wpm_screenshot. Required when space:'image' (a pre-worker refusal otherwise); an id that was already cleaned up is refused with stale_ref rather than reinterpreted.

label.description: Element number from wpm_snapshot. Act on that element through its UIA pattern instead of guessing from the point. x/y are still required and must fall inside the labelled element's rect, so 'the point is the contract' stays true.

snapId.description: The snapId the label came from. A label whose snapId has been superseded is refused with stale_ref -- element numbers are only meaningful for the frame they were printed in.

settleMs.description: How long to let the app commit its state before the effect is judged.

takeover.description: Take the takeover tier: the real cursor moves to the action point and is always restored, the focus is held until the action ends, and a three-phase HUD is mandatory. Requires the takeoverAllowed setting or the call is refused with takeover_unavailable.

takeoverMaxMs.description: Takeover only: how long the action may hold the cursor/focus.

tools.name: wpm_type
tools.description: Write text into the named window: either the first editable classic child (quiet tier) or a UIA element named by the caller (bounded-flash tier). No keystrokes are synthesized; the text is delivered through the window message or the pattern itself. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE WRITE IS READ BACK: the engine reads the control's value again (WM_GETTEXT on the message door, ValuePattern/LegacyIAccessible Current.Value on UIA) and only reports effect=readback-verified when the value it read equals the value predicted from what the control itself reported. A field that does not expose its text yields readback=unavailable and no upgrade; a value that came back different yields readbackMismatch=true while the effect stays what the write earned -- the application may legitimately reformat input, so a mismatch is data, not a refusal.

text.description: Text to write. Empty string is refused: it cannot be distinguished from a channel that silently did nothing.

elementName.description: Optional UIA Name or AutomationId of the control to write into. Naming an element forces the UIA tier, because a message tier cannot address 'the control called X'.

label.description: Element number from wpm_snapshot: write into that element through its UIA pattern. A faster, unambiguous alternative to elementName on a tree you have already read.

snapId.description: The snapId the label came from; a superseded snapId is refused with stale_ref.

replace.description: Replace the existing value instead of appending to it.

caretPosition.description: Message door only: where the caret should be before the characters are sent. 'idle' touches nothing (the caret is wherever the control left it, which for a never-focused field is position 0 -- measured). 'start' is EM_SETSEL(0,0); 'end' is EM_SETSEL(len,len) with len read from the control, because EM_SETSEL(-1,-1) is documented as document-end and measured as no-op on WinForms EDIT. On a value containing newlines the numeric end can land inside the buffer, so the result reports the requested and the applied pair and the readback judges. The UIA value channel replaces the whole value and has no caret to move: it answers caretIgnored=value-pattern instead of pretending.

settleMs.description: How long to let the app commit its state before the effect is judged.

takeover.description: Take the takeover tier: the HUD is shown, the focus is held until the action ends, and (with keyInput) text may be typed into the foreground target.

takeoverMaxMs.description: Takeover only: how long the action may hold the cursor/focus.

keyInput.description: Takeover only: 'inject' types the text with synthetic keyboard input into the foreground target, for windows with no message door and no UIA pattern (terminals). Requires keyInjectAllowed and the target in the foreground; otherwise the call is refused with keyinject_unavailable. The cursor is never moved by this path.

tools.notes_0_6_0: 0.6.0 adds readback + caretPosition and changes nothing in this refusals list: disabled targets, focus movement and a mismatching readback are reported in detail/effect, not as new codes -- they are states of the target, not errors in the call.

tools.name: wpm_focus
tools.description: Move keyboard focus to a named control inside the target, then reverse the foreground change once. This action always needs a UIA element: the message tier cannot set keyboard focus, so a window with no pattern is refused rather than clicked at a guessed coordinate.

elementName.description: UIA Name or AutomationId of the control that should hold focus.

label.description: Element number from wpm_snapshot: focus that element. A faster, unambiguous alternative to elementName on a tree you have already read.

snapId.description: The snapId the label came from; a superseded snapId is refused with stale_ref.

settleMs.description: How long to let the app commit its state before the effect is judged.

takeover.description: Take the takeover tier: the HUD is shown and the focus is held until the action ends, then restored. Requires the takeoverAllowed setting.

takeoverMaxMs.description: Takeover only: how long the action may hold the cursor/focus.

tools.name: wpm_status
tools.description: Report the engine's state and the desktop's focus table: paused flag, foreground window and pid, the control that holds keyboard focus, the age of the last human input, and the engine's stated stance. Read-only; useful before acting and after a refusal.
tools.noRefusalReason: pure query: it reads the focus table and returns it. There is no target to refuse, and inventing a refusal code for this tool would create a branch that can never be exercised.

tools.name: wpm_snapshot
tools.description: Read the target's accessibility tree as a NUMBERED element table: one line per element with a continuous `label`, its control type, name, automation id, screen rect (physical pixels) and the UIA patterns it exposes. This is the frame the model reasons on and the label it answers with -- pass `label`+`snapId` to click/type/focus instead of guessing coordinates. The labels are resolved back to the ELEMENT (by UIA RuntimeId, measured stable across queries), so an action taken by label still uses the silent UIA pattern path and never degrades into a coordinate click. Read-only: no input, no focus change, no proof window. '0 element(s)' is a real answer (measured on windows that disable UI Automation) and is reported as such, not as a failure.

hwnd.description: Target top-level window handle from wpm_windows.

maxElements.description: Hard cap on returned elements; the text then says 'truncated at N of M' and `truncated` is true. Measured trees: 71 visible elements for an 816-node Electron window, so the default is deliberately loose.

interactableOnly.description: Return only elements that expose a usable UIA pattern (the zero-cost first pass at a giant tree). Set false to see the whole visible tree, chrome included.

sinceSnapId.description: Report an incremental diff against this earlier snapId instead of re-describing every element: added / removed / changed, keyed by UIA RuntimeId. An unchanged tree produces an empty delta, which is the point -- repeating an unchanged table is the main token cost of a multi-step flow.

intent.description: What this frame is FOR (e.g. 'close the settings dialog'). It travels with the frame so a clean deciding subagent gets the goal and the numbered table together and answers with one label.

tools.name: wpm_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the target's screen rectangle to a PNG on disk and return the COORDINATE MAPPING as data: screenRect, imageSize, scale, identity, frame and dpiAware. The image is not returned inline (a plugin cannot mint an inline image block without the host's attachment service); write it to disk and read it with the host's image reader. The point of this action is not the picture -- it is that the caller never has to multiply a scale factor itself: hand the image coordinates straight back to click with space:'image' and the engine does the conversion, then still asserts that the point belongs to the target.

hwnd.description: Target top-level window handle from wpm_windows. Required unless fullScreen is true.

fullScreen.description: Capture the whole virtual screen instead of one window. Off by default on purpose: silently capturing the owner's entire desktop is exactly the kind of quiet overreach this product refuses elsewhere.

maxWidth.description: Downscale the saved image to at most this width. 0 (default) means scale=1 and identity=true -- no silent resampling, because a resized image is a CHANGED coordinate system and this action exists to make coordinates honest.

tools.name: wpm_preview
tools.description: Show the owner where a click WOULD land, without clicking: draw the AI marker at the point (when the overlay is up) and report, as text, which element sits under it (name, control type, automation id, rect). This turns an irreversible click into a reviewable one, and it makes confirmation independent of vision -- the answer is what the OS says is at that point, not a guess from a picture. Silent by construction: it writes no input queue entry, takes no focus, and produces no proof window. Use it before a destructive click, or as the confirmation step after reading a snapshot.

hwnd.description: Target top-level window handle from wpm_windows.

x.description: Screen X coordinate to preview. Must belong to the target window, otherwise the call is refused instead of reporting an element from another application.

refusalCases.note: A handle that does not identify a live window. Measured, no window is touched.

space:'image' names a shotId the engine never issued. The engine refuses instead of reinterpreting the image pixels as screen pixels -- substituting the raw numbers would click somewhere plausibly wrong, which is the failure class this code exists for. Measured: the call never reaches the door probe.

The refusal-test target is placed at 60,60, so (2,2) is outside it. A preview point that belongs to another window must be refused, not answered with that window's element: reporting 'you would click the desktop' and drawing the marker there would make the preview the one place this product guesses about a point it was not given. This is also the executable instance of `unreachable` (the two named-element-miss cases cannot run on this host: the WinForms positive control currently surfaces its controls as bare Panes through the legacy MSAA bridge, see findings.md).
A snapshot needs a live window: there is no tree to number. Same handle as the click case, and zero elements/patterns are touched.
Same reason as snapshot. fullScreen:true is the only path that does not need a window, and this case does not pass it.
A preview point that belongs to no named window has nothing to report and nothing to draw, so it refuses rather than looking up whatever application happens to own that pixel.

Pause is a server-side refusal checked before any capability, so a paused engine cannot be talked into acting by a target that looks reachable. Note it is wpm_status that stays callable while paused (a query), not the action tools.

WinForms has a message door but no UIA pattern. Naming an element suppresses the door (a message cannot address 'the control called X'), so the target is honestly unreachable rather than quietly clicked at a guessed child.
Focus requires UIA by definition; a WinForms target with no pattern must be refused, never approximated.

Decision-table instance. The flag is now wired (win.ps1 IsElevatedTarget, token integrity comparison) and measured live on Task Manager by test/integrity-probe.ps1; the engine-level case additionally runs in test/llm-action-battery.mjs whenever a high-integrity window exists at run time.

Decision-table instance, and now a conclusion verified by measurement rather than by caution: the takeover + keyInput path was measured NOT to drive this host's terminal (scripts/probe-console-inject.ps1: 242 Unicode events with the terminal in the foreground and Enter sent, nothing executed; scripts/probe-console-scan.ps1: same with layout scan codes). The code stays because its next step is still actionable -- use a target with a door.

Decision-table instance of the 2026-11-21 census: a Chromium window with renderer accessibility off walks to a tree with ZERO content elements (uTools measured one Chrome Legacy Window shell Pane, 0 interactive elements, identical across three in-place reads). Distinct from unreachable because the fix differs: nothing a re-query can find -- the app must relaunch with a11y on (--force-renderer-accessibility) or a different target must be picked. Real instance: scripts/uia-tree-content.ps1 plus a live engine call against uTools.

Decision-table instance. The UIA probe threw between the IsWindow check and the tree walk (element destroyed under the probe), so door measurement is impossible and no conclusion about the target is licensed. The engine appends the exception text to the reason as [uia: ...]. Before this code existed a thrown probe and a genuinely pattern-less target shared 'unreachable', and uiaErr arrived here as dead data.
The absence of facts must refuse, not default to the quiet branch. Unreachable through the engine (facts are always measured), so this one guards the table when it is used on its own.

Takeover was asked for but the HUD is not up. The HUD is a hard precondition, so the request is refused instead of being served silently by the quiet tier -- the point of the code is that the caller learns the request did not happen.

Injection requested with the keyInjectAllowed gate off. Measured fact behind the refusal: SendInput writes to the FOREGROUND window (scripts/probe-sendinput-unicode.ps1 arm B: text landed in the foreground window and not in the window the caller had in mind), so an unauthorised injection is refused rather than attempted.

Injection requested, gate open, but the target is not the foreground window and could not be raised. The engine refuses: blind injection would type into whatever the owner was using (same measured fact as keyinject-unavailable).

NOT covered by an executable schema case: it is a RUNTIME outcome of an interruption (HUD button / abort chord / host cancellation), and constructing one needs a live takeover in progress. test/takeover-test.ps1 covers the three interruption paths at the engine level; the reason is declared in tools.json refusals.
